title: Sharing GLAM Experience: Annoda Gobinda Public Library, Pabna, Bangladesh
content:
Wikimedia Bangladesh is starting a new GLAM initiative at Annoda Gobinda Public Library in Pabna. The project is being led by MS Sakib.

I have been working with GLAM projects in Rajshahi for a long time. So, on 10 and 11 August 2026, I travelled more than 100 kilometres from Rajshahi to Pabna. The main purpose of the visit was to exchange my GLAM experiences with Sakib. Sheikh Mehedi Hassan also joined us during the visit. It was a great opportunity to learn from each other and discuss the practical challenges of GLAM work.

I brought a CZUR ET25 Pro scanner from Rajshahi. I had used this scanner in my own GLAM work before. From now on, Sakib and Mehedi will use it for book digitization at the library. I showed them the complete scanning process through a hands-on session. I also shared some practical techniques that I learned from my own experience. Both of them are talented Wikimedians. They learned the workflow very quickly.
snippet: Wikimedia Bangladesh is starting a new GLAM initiative at Annoda Gobinda Public Library in Pabna. The project is being led by MS Sakib.

title: UNESCO and Wikimedia Movement Deepen Their Partnership at Wikimania 2026
content:
Wikimania 2026 in Paris marked an important step forward in the growing relationship between the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) and the Wikimedia movement. Building on grassroots partnerships developed with UNESCO field offices, Wikimedia Foundation staff and Wikimédia France helped connect regional collaboration with colleagues at UNESCO headquarters, creating new opportunities for stronger institutional engagement.

Together with Alejandra Reyes (Wikimedia France), Michael David Miller (Université McGill et Wikimedia Canada) the Wikimania 2026 chair and co-chair of the Partners and Sponsors Committee, and Sakti Pramudya (Wikimedia Foundation), they formed a team that supported the coordination of these engagements, helping demonstrate how trust and partnerships developed at the local and regional levels can contribute to broader collaboration globally.
snippet: Wikimania 2026 in Paris marked an important step forward in the growing relationship between the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) and the Wikimedia movement.

title: Call for Satellite Hosts: Wiki Indaba Hackathon 2026
content:
The Wiki Indaba Hackathon Committee is inviting Wikimedia communities, affiliates, user groups, universities, technology communities, and other organisations across Africa to host satellite locations for the Wiki Indaba Hackathon 13th to 15th November 2026.

A Satellite location is a space that will allow participants who cannot attend the main event in person to gather locally, collaborate on projects, and connect with the wider hackathon online.

We are looking for hosts who can provide:

  • A suitable space for participants for 2 to 3 days
  • Reliable internet connectivity for 2 to 3 days
  • Electricity or a power backup solution
  • A local person who can coordinate the satellite location
  • Basic coordination with the organising team

    • You do not need to have hosted a hackathon before. What matters most is having a suitable space, a reliable local contact, and an interest in supporting the Wikimedia technical community.

    Satellite hosts will:

  • Coordinate the local venue and participants
  • Ensure the space and connectivity are ready
  • Stay in contact with the Satellite Coordination Lead
  • Support participants during the hackathon
  • Help connect the local group with the main hackathon programme
snippet: The Wiki Indaba Hackathon Committee is inviting Wikimedia communities, affiliates, user groups, universities, technology communities, and other organisations across Africa to host satellite locations

title: ESEAP Conference 2026: Reflection from My First Time Attending and Growing within the Wikimedia Movement
content:
Since WikiTraining introduced me to Wikipedia and opened my eyes to broader Wikimedia projects back in 2018, my journey with the Wikimedia movement has been deeply fulfilling. For years, I’ve been actively involved in various community initiatives, with a strong focus on enriching content for the Sundanese language Wikimedia project. I was completely comfortable creating impact in my familiar space, never expecting to be given such a meaningful opportunity. However, I eventually realized that to grow further and bring more value to my local community, I needed to expand my inner world. It was that very desire that pushed me out of my comfort zone to apply for a scholarship to my first international conference (the ESEAP Conference 2026).

Little did I know that single step of courage would bring an abundance of unexpected opportunities. Beyond receiving the scholarship, our presentation proposal was also selected, giving us space to share our project “WikiTutuwuhan”, an initiative documenting the botany of West Java. This is my reflection on stepping into something greater and growing within the Wikimedia movement.

title: Tech News 2026 – Issue 34
content:
Latest tech news from the Wikimedia technical community. Please tell other users about these changes. Not all changes will affect you. Translations are available.

Weekly highlight

  • The Worklist feature for the Event Registration tool is now live on all Wikimedia wikis. With Worklist, event organizers can add the articles their event will focus on directly to the event page. The Worklist also powers Event Pathways which notifies other editors of the upcoming or ongoing event when they edit an article featured in the event’s Worklist. This is the minimum viable version (MVP), and feedback is welcome. Organizers are encouraged to try the feature. A hands-on Worklist Setup Workshop will take place on 18 August at 16:00 UTC and 19 August at 11:00 UTC.

    • Updates for editors

  • Special:ShortPages displays short pages by their size, but in many cases it gets filled with disambiguations and soft redirects, making it harder to find the short articles themselves. Starting this weekend, you will be able to choose not to include an article in the special page by adding the magic word __EXPECTSHORTPAGE__. [1]
  • One new wiki has been created: a Wikipedia in Bole (w:bol:) [2]

title: Historic delegation from Wikimedia Chile participates in Wikimania Paris in preparation for Santiago 2027
content:
Wikimania Paris 2026 brought together around 3,000 people from around the world, 1,200 of whom attended in person, to celebrate Wikipedia’s 25th anniversary and discuss the challenges and opportunities facing the Wikimedia movement.

Under the theme “Freedom, Equity, and Reliability” (Liberté, Équité, Fiabilité). “Together, let’s protect knowledge, equity, and freedom,” the conference sparked discussions around fundamental questions for the movement: How can we resist political and media attacks against free knowledge? How can we strengthen solidarity among multilingual Wikimedia communities and other digital commons? And how can we ensure increasingly inclusive spaces where people can imagine and build the future together?

In this context, Wikimedia Chile was represented by a delegation of 15 members—the largest in our organization’s history—including our members Dennis Tobar, Claudio Loader, Sebastián Flores, Luis Carrasco, Carlos Figueroa, Daniela Colleoni, Nicole González, and Céline Assémat.

content:

Eugene Ormandy：I felt encouraged to see that, in 2026, efforts to archive culture and host editing events (edit-a-thons) for Wikimedia projects across the ESEAP region were proceeding smoothly.
　I also gave two presentations this time: the first was a lightning talk on the Wikimedia movement among Japanese GLAM sector, and the second was a panel discussion on the Wikimedia in education: a look at Wiki Clubs. I hope both sessions served as an opportunity for an international audience to learn about the situation in Japan. For the latter session, I appeared alongside young people from Japan; they were all highly capable, which gave me great peace of mind.
　It was also a pleasure to reunite with friends from abroad. I was especially happy to see Alan Ang again after such a long time; we caught up on each other’s recent news and exchanged views on topics such as the significance of Wikidata in the age of AI and MCP integration.

title: From Baghdad to Paris: Celebrating the Past and Shaping Wikimedia’s Future at Wikimania 2026
content:
From July 21 to July 25, 2026, I had the opportunity to participate in Wikimania 2026 at the Cité des Sciences et de l’Industrie in Paris, France. This year’s Wikimania, the 21st edition of the global Wikimedia conference, brought Wikimedians together under the theme “Freedom, Equity, Reliability” and was also part of the celebration of 25 years of Wikipedia.

This Wikimania felt particularly special. Celebrating the 25th birthday of Wikipedia surrounded by Wikimedians from around the world was a reminder of how far a project that started with a simple but ambitious idea has come. Seeing the Baby Globe around the conference, joining the celebrations, and hearing the stories of contributors from different generations made the anniversary feel much more than just a number. It was a celebration of 25 years of people working together to make knowledge freely accessible.

title: Supporting Bangla Wikipedia’s Front Page: My Journey as a “Did You Know?” Administrator
content:
Wikipedia’s Main Page is often the first stop for readers seeking knowledge. While millions of people see the finished product every day, few realize the collaborative work that happens behind the scenes to keep it accurate, engaging, and constantly refreshed.

One of the most visible spaces on Bangla Wikipedia’s Main Page is “আপনি জানেন কী?” (“Did You Know?”), a section that showcases fascinating facts from recently created or significantly expanded articles. Each fact invites readers to discover something unexpected while encouraging contributors to improve the encyclopedia’s content.

In August 2025, I had the privilege of joining the team responsible for managing this section, becoming the second volunteer entrusted with maintaining one of Bangla Wikipedia’s most frequently visited pages.

For several years, the “Did You Know?” section had been managed by Faisal Bin Darul, who single-handedly reviewed nominations, verified articles, and prepared new facts for publication. As Bangla Wikipedia continued to grow, the community recognized the need to share this responsibility to ensure that the section remained active and regularly updated.

title: WikiRempah Betawi Building Leadership from Batavia to Moloku Kie Raha
content:
Jakarta has long been a meeting point, from the era of Sunda Kelapa to Batavia. For centuries, the city served as a port where cultures from across the Indonesian archipelago came together.

Together with Hzu Hzu, Affandy Murad, Bangrapip, Kume Gucci, and Li Ersha, the Wikimedia Jakarta Community began the WikiRempah program initiated by Ana Ainina, Supardi Sahabu, and Sofi Solihah. 

Oceanmuse | CC-BY SA 4.0

WikiRempah is an initiative funded through the Wikimedia Foundation‘s Rapid Funds program and carried out in collaboration with communities supported by Wikimedia Indonesia.

Working alongside local communities across Indonesia, the initiative consists of field documentation, article development, dictionary entries, and recordings of local dialects, all of which will be made openly accessible through Wikimedia projects.

Far from Maluku, Yet Its Flavors Can Still Be Found in Jakarta

Far from Maluku, Yet Its Flavors Can Still Be Found in Jakarta

The presence of Maluku restaurants in Jakarta gave us an opportunity to introduce the richness of Maluku’s spices to more people without geographical barriers.

title: EduWiki at Wikimania 2026: AI, Big Ideas, and Our First In-Person Workshop
content:
Wikimania 2026 brought the Wikimedia community together in Paris, and EduWiki was part of the week with two sessions centred on education.

On 22 July, the panel on AI and Wikipedia in Education: Opportunities, Ethics, and Equity in Practice brought 60 educators and Wikimedia programme leaders together to discuss how artificial intelligence is already affecting teaching and learning. On 24 July, the EduWiki Hub held its first in-person workshop, where 30 participants worked in groups of five to design impactful Wikimedia education activities around real situations in the Wikimedia and Education ecosystem.

Both sessions drew from experiences people are already having in classrooms, programmes, and Wikimedia communities.

Around 60 participants joined AI and Wikipedia in Education: Opportunities, Ethics, and Equity in Practice.

Moderated by Filip Maljković, the panel featured Jackie Bucio from the National Autonomous University of Mexico, LiAnna Davis from Wiki Education, and Luisina Ferrante from Wikimedia Argentina.
snippet: Wikimania 2026 brought the Wikimedia community together in Paris, and EduWiki was part of the week with two sessions centred on education.

title: From Wiki Batu Basurek to Wiki Prasasti: Saving Ancient Inscriptions Through Quality Wikipedia Articles
content:
In the world of the open Wikimedia movement, we often find ourselves trapped in metrics: how many thousands of new articles were created this week? But what is the value of thousands of articles if they end up as a “fleeting glimpse of shallow information”—consisting of merely two stub paragraphs with minimal citations?

In this project (batu basurek is the Minangkabau term for ancient inscriptions), we chose a more challenging path: focusing on quality. We completed and enriched stub articles about 13th and 14th-century inscriptions in West Sumatra province, Indonesia, transforming them from basic two-paragraph stubs into comprehensive documentation—complete with transliteration, historical analysis, verified academic references, and updated photography.

Why is documenting these inscriptions so crucial? The answer lies in the field.

title: Working with the Visual Editor within Outreachy
content:
Continuing our work in the wish #3 of the Lusophone Technological Wishlist within the 32nd round of Outreachy…

Over the past weeks, development focused on MediaWiki, Visual Editor and their core extension ecosystem. While the validation logic itself was initially expected to be straightforward, configuring the local ecosystem presented the first major complexity. Setting up VisualEditor, Citoid, and Cite locally required carefully identifying and setting up the exact suite of dependencies needed to replicate Wikipedia’s production environment.

Following mentor recommendations, the setup was built using a Wikimedia dockerized environment. To ensure accurate citation formatting and parsing, the following extensions were required to integrate:

  • Cite, Citoid which are required to search, retrieve, and translate inputs (ISBN, DOI, or URL) into reference nodes.
  • TemplateData, Scribunto, TemplateStyles to support structured citation template rendering.

title: Celebrating the Art and Feminism Writing Challenge 2026
content:
The Dagbani Wikimedians User Group successfully organized the Art and Feminism Writing Challenge 2026 across three of its active Wiki Hubs, namely the Bimbico Wiki Hub, the TACE Wiki Hub, and the BACE Wiki Hub. The challenge was held from July 19th to August 3rd, 2026, bringing together passionate volunteers who worked diligently to improve the coverage of women on Wikimedia platforms.

The challenge specifically focused on women in the healthcare sector. Participants created and improved articles about notable women whose work and achievements have made significant contributions to healthcare, medicine, nursing, public health, medical research, and related fields. Through this initiative, contributors helped address the gender gap in online knowledge by ensuring that the stories and accomplishments of these remarkable women were better documented and made freely accessible to people around the world.

title: Wiki Town: Playas Doradas, Patagonia Argentina
content:
The community embraced the project and completed the installation of QR codes that link to Wikipedia articles. 

On July 25, residents of Playas Doradas (Río Negro, Argentina) walked through the town’s streets installing 38 new QR codes on street signs. Each code links a street name to the Wikipedia article about the species that gives it its name:trofón, buccino, jarillal, piquillines, among other plants and animals native to the Patagonian steppe. The event marked the conclusion of a phase of the project “Las calles de Playas Doradas”, (The Streets of Playas Doradas) spearheaded by WikiUNLP in collaboration with La Lechuza Community Library, Islote Lobos National Park (National Parks Administration), and Sierra Grande Department of Tourism. The project achieved something that doesn’t always happen: a community that embraced the initiative as its own
